title: Constructible models for duals of locally constant perfect complexes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and let $S$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the admissible condensed coefficient rings $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $A$ is finite commutative and killed by a power of $\ell$ and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $R=\Lambda(*)$ and $B=\Lambda_S$. Use the pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], scalar perfect complexes [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex, def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], and the relative unbounded derived tensor and internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Suppose $P\in D(B)$ has a pro-étale cover $\{U_i\to S\}$ and bounded complexes $F_i^\bullet$ of finite projective $R$-modules such that $P|_{U_i}\simeq B|_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{F_i^\bullet}$, with termwise tensor and constant sheaves denoted by underlines. Set $P^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_B(P,B)$ and $F_i^{\vee,\bullet}=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(F_i^\bullet,R[0])$. For every integer $q$ there are isomorphisms
$$H^q(P)|_{U_i}\cong B|_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{H^q(F_i^\bullet)},\qquad H^q(P^\vee)|_{U_i}\cong B|_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{H^q(F_i^{\vee,\bullet})}.$$
The scalar cohomology modules in these formulas are finitely presented. Both $P$ and $P^\vee$ have bounded cohomology and belong to $\Dbc(S,\Lambda)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The assertion includes the completed integral coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,S}\cong\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_S$ [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit, lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction].

source.place: Paragraph 2, final sentence (locally constant perfect coefficient dual); paragraph 3, parenthetical assertion that the perfect factors lie in Dctf: extracted scalar-cohomology part.

proof.text: The scalar ring $R$ is Noetherian. For finite $A$, every ideal is generated by its finite underlying set; for a field, an ideal is either zero or generated by $1$. For $R=\mathcal O_E$, [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr](2) says every ideal is principal; $R=\mathbf Z_\ell$ is the case $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, with its valuation ring identified in [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. These statements give the ideal-finiteness definition [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] in every admissible scalar case, including $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

source.place: Definition of Noetherian ring; blueprint local scalar models; coefficient DVR property from the cited node.

proof.text: By [lem-sf-finite-projective-dual], each $\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_i^{-q},R)$ is finite projective. Thus $F_i^{\vee,\bullet}$ is bounded, in $[-b_i,-a_i]$ if $F_i$ is supported in $[a_i,b_i]$. For either scalar complex $G=F_i$ or $F_i^\vee$, apply [lem-pc-noetherian-finite-kernels-cokernels] to $d^q:G^q\to G^{q+1}$ to see that $Z^q(G)$ is finite. Apply its cokernel clause to $G^{q-1}\to Z^q(G)$ to see that $H^q(G)$ is finite. Step 1 and [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation] make it finitely presented. This does not assert that cohomology is projective: finite coefficient rings need not be regular.

source.place: Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation (1),(2); more-algebra.tex Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, termwise dual.

proof.text: On any scheme $T$, write $C_T(M)=\Lambda_T\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$. For finite $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] identifies its condensed ring with the constant ring on the point. The inverse image $p_T^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] preserves finite coproducts and the terminal object; thus it takes this finite constant ring to $\underline A$, including its operations. Hence $C_T$ is the exact constant module functor of [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]. If $R$ is one of the field stages, every short exact sequence of $R$-vector spaces splits: choose a basis of the quotient using [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector], lift each basis vector, and extend linearly to a section. Applying $C_T$ preserves this splitting and the finite direct-sum decomposition. Hence $C_T$ is exact on scalar modules for every field stage, including the specified condensed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. This argument does not identify $\Lambda_T$ with the discrete constant field sheaf.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; field case: agent splitting argument using the cited basis theorem.

proof.text: For $R=\mathcal O_E$, [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit](3) identifies $\Lambda_T$ with $\varprojlim_n\underline{R/\pi_E^n}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] with $A=R$ and $I=(\pi_E)$: its hypotheses hold by Step 1. It makes this completed sheaf flat over $\underline R$. Composing tensor with this flat sheaf with the exact constant module functor gives exactness of $C_T$. The same proof with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ handles $\mathbf Z_\ell$. Thus $C_T$ is exact in every coefficient case. This uses flatness of completion, not an assertion that inverse limits of arbitrary exact sequences are exact.

source.place: Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat; Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; blueprint integral-limit identification.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and put $E_i^\bullet=C_{U_i}(F_i^\bullet)$ and $B_i=B|_{U_i}$. The finite-projective splittings of [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] remain splittings after constant realization and scalar extension: each $E_i^q$ is a direct summand of some $B_i^{N_q}$. By [lem-sc-finite-free-internal-hom-exact], $\mathcal Hom_{B_i}(B_i^{N_q},-)$ is exact. Its natural idempotent $h\mapsto h\circ(i_qp_q)$ has image $\mathcal Hom_{B_i}(E_i^q,-)$. An exact sequence with such a commuting idempotent is the direct sum of its image and complementary image sequences; equivalently, applying the idempotent to a local lift gives a lift in its image. Therefore the image sequence is exact too. This proves the termwise internal-Hom exactness needed in the next step.

source.place: Tag 08JH, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect: finite-free-summand terms; elementary splitting of an exact sequence by a natural idempotent.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], $P^\vee|_{U_i}\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{B_i}(E_i^\bullet,B_i)$. In the K-injective definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], choose $B_i[0]\to I_i^\bullet$. Step 5 verifies every hypothesis of [lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso] for the bounded complex $E_i$: the map $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E_i,B_i[0])\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E_i,I_i^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently $P^\vee|_{U_i}$ is represented by the ordinary dual complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{B_i}(E_i^\bullet,B_i[0])$. No global projectivity of module sheaves is being inferred from their finite-projective local splittings.

source.place: Tags 08JB and 08JH, lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U and lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect; bounded Hom invariance is cited in its ringed-site form.

proof.text: For each finite projective $R$-module $V$, define $\beta_V:C_{U_i}(\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R))\to\mathcal Hom_{B_i}(C_{U_i}(V),B_i)$ by $\beta_V(b\otimes\phi)(b'\otimes v)=bb'\phi(v)$. For $V=R^N$ it is the usual identification of both sides with $B_i^N$. For the splitting $V\xrightarrow{i}R^N\xrightarrow{p}V$, naturality carries precomposition with $ip$ on the free dual to the same idempotent on the sheaf dual; restricting the free isomorphism to the images gives an inverse for $\beta_V$. Thus $\beta_V$ is an isomorphism, natural in $V$. In degree $q$, apply it to $V=F_i^{-q}$. Both dual differentials send $\phi$ to $-(-1)^q\phi d_F$, by [def-pur-hom-complex], so naturality makes these degreewise isomorphisms a chain isomorphism. Step 6 therefore gives $P^\vee|_{U_i}\simeq C_{U_i}(F_i^{\vee,\bullet})$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, final finite-free-retract calculation; explicit scalar base-change identification and Hom differential.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](c) to the exact functor $C_{U_i}$ of Steps 3--4, first for $F_i$ and then for $F_i^\vee$. Apply it also to exact slice restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], so that taking $H^q$ commutes with restriction to $U_i$. The given model for $P$ and the model from Step 7 then give, on every original covering object and for every integer $q$,
$$H^q(P)|_{U_i}\cong C_{U_i}(H^q(F_i)),\qquad H^q(P^\vee)|_{U_i}\cong C_{U_i}(H^q(F_i^\vee)).$$
Step 2 supplies the required finite presentation of both scalar modules. In particular these are the original covering objects, not just the finite refinement used below.

source.place: Tag 010N, exact functors preserve kernels and cokernels, hence images and homology; sites-modules.tex exact slice restriction.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian by the ideal argument of Step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $S$ Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact. It is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Choose a finite affine open cover of $S$ by quasi-compactness and apply [lem-sfb-finite-affine-proetale-refinement] to the original covering. This gives a finite covering family $\{V_j\to S\}_{j=1}^n$, with each $V_j\to S$ factoring through some original $U_{i(j)}$. The coefficient identification and exact pullback of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] restrict the two local models and their scalar formulas to this finite family. For $S=\varnothing$ both complexes and all their sheaves are zero, and the assertion follows with bound $[0,0]$; assume henceforth that $S$ is nonempty.

source.place: Paragraph 3, membership of the perfect factors; finite refinement and global bounds as expanded in det-prop-scalar-six-ctf.proof.md (2).

proof.text: Choose intervals $[a_j,b_j]$ supporting $F_{i(j)}$ and put $a=\min_j a_j$, $b=\max_j b_j$, enlarging zero-complex intervals if necessary. On the finite cover, the models for $P$ are supported in $[a,b]$ and those for $P^\vee$ in $[-b,-a]$. Apply [lem-sfb-local-model-cohomology-descent] twice: exactness of its scalar functors was proved in Steps 3--4 and finite presentation in Step 2. It gives global cohomology bounds in these intervals and constructibility of every cohomology sheaf on the single stratum $S$. Equivalently, the original-cover formulas of Step 8 already give the finite constant local models required by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; the finite cover supplies only the uniform bound. Thus both objects belong to $\Dbc(S,\Lambda)$, with the completed integral coefficient sheaf retained throughout.

tool_uses.why: Coefficient DVR theorem gives principal ideals for integral scalar rings, hence Noetherianity; no stability theorem is used.
Generic finite-discrete condensed ring identification is used to identify the finite coefficient sheaf with the constant ring, before exactness of the constant module functor.
Coefficient-specific inverse-limit identification supplies the actual completed integral coefficient sheaf, before applying completion-flatness.
Cartesian coefficient identification and exact inverse image restrict the local scalar models to the finite refinement.
Generic completion-flatness theorem supplies exact scalar extension for the integral coefficients; the unit does not give this flatness fact.
Generic ringed-site finite-free Hom exactness supplies the finite-summand calculation, without any scheme structure-sheaf specialization.
Generic ringed-site derived Hom restriction identifies the local dual with the restricted global dual.
Generic bounded Hom invariance for sheaf-module complexes proves that the ordinary dual represents derived Hom.
Generic exact restriction to a slice site is needed to commute cohomology with the original cover.
Generic finite pro-etale cover refinement from the scalar-six unit supplies the uniform bounds for the same scalar-perfect local models.
Generic finite-cover descent from the scalar-six unit supplies boundedness and constructibility once exactness and finite scalar cohomology are verified.

lean.statement: theorem internalHomDual_constructible_models (l p : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) (hpl : p ≠ l) (S : Scheme.{u}) [S.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (S ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (S ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (S ↘ Spec (.of k))] : (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A], (∃ n : ℕ, (l : A) ^ n = 0) → Assertion A (finiteCoefficients A) (finiteModel A) S) ∧ Assertion (ULift.{u} ℤ_[l]) (baseIntegralCoefficients l) (baseIntegralModel l) S ∧ (∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E], Assertion (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E) (FiniteConstantModel.integralCoefficients l E) (FiniteConstantModel.integralModel l E) S) ∧ Assertion (ULift.{u} ℚ_[l]) (baseRationalCoefficients l) (baseRationalModel l) S ∧ (∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E], Assertion E (FiniteConstantModel.rationalCoefficients l E) (FiniteConstantModel.rationalModel l E) S) ∧ Assertion (ULift.{u} (PadicAlgCl l)) (algebraicCoefficients l) (algebraicModel l) S
lean.note: Six explicit coefficient cases of the single local-model assertion: finite discrete A, Z_l, O_E, Q_l, E, and Qbar_l. Ordinary scalar realization reuses FiniteConstantModelResolution. Maintainer review fix: the Qbar_l case is the continuous condensed ring C(-,Qbar_l) for the l-adic norm topology (sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; the coefficient convention of sk-def-localizing-closure, IsLocalizingAdmissibleCoefficient), realized by the same canonical modelFunctor as the other cases, replacing the delivered finite-subextension colimit object padicAlgClRingObj. The ordinary signed scalar dual is given by real degreewise data. ULift on the three Type-0 base rings only transports scalar coordinates to the scheme universe; all scalar module objects live in Type (u+1). No assumptions of scalar exactness, dualizability or constructibility are added.
